html:
In 1691 at Dolon Nor, in Inner Mongolia, the princes of the Khalkha Mongols, who held what is now Mongolia, swore loyalty to the Kangxi Emperor of the Qing dynasty.

They had been routed by Galdan of the Dzungars in 1688 and fled south. Their spiritual leader, Zanabazar, urged them to choose the Qing as protectors. Kangxi then defeated Galdan in 1696.

The Khalkha became a Qing frontier, Outer Mongolia, ruled through their own princes and Buddhist monasteries. Trade debts to Chinese merchants and the spread of monastic life marked the next two centuries. When the Qing fell in 1911, the Mongols declared independence under the Bogd Khan.
sum: In 1691 at Dolon Nor, in Inner Mongolia, the princes of the Khalkha Mongols, who held what is now Mongolia, swore loyalty to the Kangxi Emperor of the Qing dynasty.
